## /rebar-debug RCA — mechanism PROVEN; legitimacy classified NOT-A-BUG (feature-request). No fix applied.

Investigated at origin/main `0b851c8103` in an isolated worktree. Phase 1 completed; the Phase-2
not-a-bug guard held, so **no code change was made** and the disposition is handed to a human.

### Proven mechanism (confirmed by runtime measurement, not by reading source)

A gate op is a multi-phase pipeline; **no component emits anything between command start and the
final verdict at the default log level**. Three contributing facts, all confirmed:

1. **The two longest phases have NO instrumentation at any level.** Measured at
   `REBAR_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` (rebar's most verbose setting) on `review-plan --force`, total 130.4s:
   - `t+0 -> t+27.1` = **27.1s** silent — material-assembly / store-hydration prologue.
   - `t+52.2 -> t+92.2` = **40.0s** silent — overlap-corpus retrieval
     (`overlap corpus: 852 fresh digests, 3833 skipped`). Pure LOCAL compute, no model call.
2. **The phase logs that do exist are INFO and fire AFTER their phase completes**, never at its
   start: `llm/plan_review/pass1.py:274`, `llm/workflow/container_stage.py:189,235,290`,
   `llm/agent_call.py:381`. The default level is WARNING (`_logging.py:_resolve_level`, :91-100),
   overridable only by `REBAR_LOG_LEVEL` — there is no `--verbose` that raises it.
3. **The sole shared LLM seam emits nothing during the call.** Every gate op funnels through
   `PydanticAIRunner.run` (`llm/runner.py:296`); the leaves are non-streaming
   `agent.run_sync` (`llm/runner.py:540`, `llm/structured_run.py:211`, `:249`). `run_stream` has
   NEVER existed in `src/rebar/llm/` (`git log -S'run_stream'` => zero commits).

### Discriminating experiments (3 runs, same worktree/ticket)

| run | level | LLM | silent prologue | largest later gap | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | WARNING (default) | fresh | 54.2s | **85.4s** to verdict | 146.9s |
| 2 | DEBUG | none (reuse path) | 27.2s | — | 27.4s |
| 3 | DEBUG | forced fresh | 27.1s | **40.0s** (overlap retrieval) | 130.4s |

- Run 1 vs Run 3 **rejects** "the signals exist but sit below the default level": raising the level
  reveals per-call lines, yet 27s and 40s holes remain, so those phases have nothing to suppress.
- Run 2 **rejects** "the silence is the model call": it made no model call and was still silent for
  27.2s (11.9s user + 13.0s system of real work).
- Run 1's own verdict reports `llm_ms: 13047` of a **146,900 ms** wall clock — the model is ~9% of
  the run. A streaming-only remedy (the ticket's remedy #2) would therefore NOT break the failure.

Emission plumbing is NOT the gap: run 1's three `enrich_drain` WARNINGs arrived through a pipe
85s before exit, proving `logging`->stderr already flushes promptly mid-run. Nothing chooses to write.

### Legitimacy: `feature-request` — cited, and this is why no fix was applied

Progress emission on gate ops was never built and never removed (not a regression). The
long-silent-run behaviour is, by contrast, **deliberate and recorded twice**:

- **ADR 0089 — "Activity-based liveness under run_sync; async idle-watchdog deferred"** (Accepted
  2026-07-09, ~1 month old, so it states CURRENT intent): LLM gate runs' *"time-to-first-token can
  legitimately be minutes of silence"*; *"No total-runtime timeout anywhere in the gate path"*; the
  reset-on-event stream watchdog *"is NOT built"*, deferred behind a stated trigger (migrating the
  runner to async `agent.run()`), which is unmet. Restated at `docs/config.md:402-406`.
- **`docs/plan-review-gate.md:1415-1424`, section "End-to-end time-to-first-work (honest)"**: the
  review *"takes seconds to minutes depending on ticket size + tier"* and *"no upfront wall-clock
  benchmark is claimed"* — a deliberate refusal, which is what AC-2 of this ticket asks to reverse.

No doc, test, or contract requires a gate op to emit progress or bound its silence. Under the
protocol's three-way test this is "never built, and nothing shows it was designed" =>
**feature-request**, which is fail-closed: a human decides, rather than an agent patching it in.

### Honest counter-argument (why this is not a slam dunk)

ADR 0089's subject is INBOUND liveness — how rebar bounds a hung *model*. It never posed the
outbound question "should rebar announce it is alive?" And its "time-to-first-token" justification
does not reach the two dominant holes, which are **local compute** (27s prologue, 40s overlap
retrieval) with no recorded justification at all. A reviewer could fairly read those two phases as
an unjustified gap rather than an intended design. That is the strongest case for `defect`; it did
not clear the bar of a *cited* authoritative source, so the guard held.

### Recommended disposition (for a human to accept or reject)

1. **Cheapest effective remedy, and ADR 0089 does NOT block it.** The ADR deferred a *stream-event
   idle watchdog* (kills a stalled run; needs async). A *periodic liveness emitter* is a different
   mechanism and is already proven compatible with blocking sync code in this repo:
   `_engine/rebar_reconciler/_heartbeat.py:52-93` runs `threading.Thread(daemon=True)` +
   `stop.wait(interval)`. A ~30s heartbeat to stderr wrapping the gate op would break the failure.
   Natural seams, coarse to fine: `llm/workflow/executor.py:641` (per workflow step),
   `llm/runner.py:296` (per LLM call), `llm/agent_call.py:178,202` (per tool call).
   Constraint: `src/rebar/llm/**` is NOT on the ruff T201 print allowlist (`pyproject.toml:399-440`),
   so it must go through `logging`, not `print`.
2. **Re-scope AC-2.** It asks docs to state an expected duration range, but
   `docs/plan-review-gate.md:1420-1424` deliberately declines to claim a benchmark. The
   defensible doc change is not a benchmark but a **warning that gate ops routinely exceed common
   600s supervisor stall budgets while silent**, plus how to raise them. Note `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S`
   is itself `600` (`llm/config.py:124`) *per request*, and the close path can issue many requests
   (`close_autoresume.py:191` is a `while True` up to `verify.auto_resume_max`), so worst-case
   wall clock is a large multiple of the very budget that killed the reporting agent.
3. If accepted, this should be re-typed from `bug` to a feature/task and given acceptance criteria
   naming a proving command, per the advisory findings its own plan review returned (P1/P9/P10).

No files were changed. Worktree retired.
